items.description: We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want. You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models. Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week. How it works Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume. Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate. Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks. Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them. Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it. Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round. Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another. Requirements 2+ years of professional software engineering Code merged into a public open-source repository, ideally one you know well. A private codebase you own may also qualify (not employer or client code) Strong in at least one of Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java or C++ Solid with Docker, Linux, Git and automated testing Regular use of an AI coding tool Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words At least 10 hours a week, starting now A secure personal or work computer (no public or shared machines) Nice to have Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure Experience building agent tasks or RL environments Terms US$1,000 for each task that passes our quality review, paid directly to you Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms The work is used for AI training. The change and your solution must be your own, and you must be free to license them to us Don't publish the work anywhere: no public pull request or public fork Apply at https://www.askable.com/experts/roles/senior-software-engineer Location: Worldwide Job type: contract

items.description: ð Build the data layer AI needs to do science Application deadline: 16 Nov 2026 23:59 CET About Claims AI ate the Internet, but it can't digest science yet. A paper is thousands of words of prose written for humans, but an AI agent doing research needs to know what was claimed, what evidence supports it, and how far to trust it. Claims turns the scientific literature into exactly that: every claim, tied to its evidence, as structured data that models and agents can query. We're a startup and run as Subnet 111 on Bittensor. Since our mainnet launch on 28 August 2026, an open competition of miners has processed more than 10,000 papers, and every record was checked by our validator before it entered the dataset. The competition keeps raising the bar: miners keep finding ways to beat our own reference pipeline, and every win becomes part of the standard the whole network is scored against. The team Claims was founded by two professors of economics and a senior engineer. Philipp Koellinger , CEO, is a professor of economics and an experienced entrepreneur: founder of DeSci Labs and the DeSci Foundation, and co-builder of SciWeave with Ogban. Christian Roessler , co-founder, is a professor of economics and game theorist. He designs the incentive mechanism that makes the miner competition work. Ogban Ugot , engineering, is a senior backend and machine learning engineer. He built SciWeave, the Claims miner, validator and data pipeline, and you will work with him every day. You would be the fourth person on the team and our second engineer. Our culture We are a fully remote team spread across Europe, Africa and the US West Coast. We have a flat hierarchy and move fast towards clearly defined goals. We think deep, don't shy away from difficult problems or conversations, and we ship relentlessly. The code you will write will run on a live network within your first weeks, and you own real things from day one. You need to be able to join our team meetings in the afternoon, Central European Time. Type: Full-time contractor. Start in December 2026 or January 2027. Attack triage: identify patterns across country, carrier, number range, device and attestation signals; separate SMS pumping, bot traffic and account abuse from legitimate spikes. Threshold tuning: analyse and backtest anti-fraud rules and thresholds; quantify false positives (legitimate users blocked) against fraud prevented; recommend changes with evidence. Detection and monitoring: turn recurring forensics into scheduled queries, dashboards and alerts so attacks are caught in hours, not after the provider invoice. Engineering hand-off: give backend engineers precise, ready-to-implement rule proposals so they stay focused on platform delivery. Knowledge transfer: document playbooks and coach our analytics engineer so capability stays in the team. Requirements Mandatory 5+ years in analytics engineering, data science or fraud analytics, with at least 2 years hands-on in fraud or abuse detection. Building scheduled pipelines in Airflow and dashboards in Looker (or equivalent BI). Experience tuning rule- or threshold-based fraud controls, including backtesting and false-positive analysis.

items.description: Contract Duration: 12 months Engagement: Full-time contract Location: Remote, Mexico, Colombia, Argentina Project Objective Our client is looking for a senior, hands-on Data Architect / Engineer to lead the design and delivery of an analytical data platform in Microsoft Fabric. The objective is to offload historical and analytical workloads from a core transactional product into a secure, governed analytical data store. The solution must preserve the authorization context required for downstream consumption, support customer-facing reporting, and establish a foundation for future data products. You will own the technical delivery of this initiative, working with internal teams and external technical partners from discovery and architecture through implementation, production readiness, documentation, and knowledge transfer. Key Outcomes Deliver a production-ready architecture that separates transactional and analytical workloads. Design and implement ingestion and historical offload from Azure-based transactional databases into Microsoft Fabric. Establish a layered or medallion architecture covering source-aligned, transformed, and consumption-ready data. Create analytical and semantic models that support secure downstream reporting and customer-facing use cases. Understand the application's roles, permissions, and visibility rules, and translate the required authorization context into appropriate analytical access patterns. Design for historical preservation, change handling, retention, deletions, reconciliation, and future transactional data purging. Implement the engineering controls required for production operation, including testing, data quality, monitoring, recovery, security, and deployment. Assess the existing ingestion and analytical processes, retaining what works and improving or replacing what does not. Maintain clear technical documentation, architecture decisions, operational runbooks, and implementation knowledge throughout the engagement. Transfer knowledge to the internal Data & Analytics team so the platform can be operated and extended after the contract. Required Experience Senior-level experience delivering data architecture and data-engineering solutions in production environments. Proven experience transforming data from complex OLTP applications into analytical platforms, data warehouses, lakehouses, or OLAP solutions. You'll design and train damage detection models while architecting the high-throughput serving infrastructure needed to keep those models performant under real production loads. As ACV continues to grow, you'll play a direct role in ensuring our inspection capabilities remain accurate, efficient, and resilient at scale. This role goes beyond executing on a defined roadmap. You'll identify opportunities, shape solutions end-to-end, and take ownership of outcomes. You connect the dots between stakeholder needs and what's technically feasible, bringing recommendations grounded in both theory and practical constraints. When you hear a narrow question, you think about the broader system it lives in and build toward that. Architect and maintain high-throughput, containerized microservices for model serving using REST/gRPC to ensure low-latency performance. Proficiency in Go, Python and shell, and comfort building the tooling rather than only using it. Position Summary: The Applied Artificial Intelligence Engineer is part of the Education Design and Informatics team within the Office of Health Sciences Education at Vanderbilt University School of Medicine. You'll be our first dedicated AI/ML role, working alongside a data engineer, full-stack developers, and instructional designers to build intelligent features into our products. Near-term priorities include LLM-powered tools for learners and educators, semantic search across educational content, recommendation systems for personalized learning pathways, and integration of AI capabilities into VSTAR. As our AI maturity grows, you'll also contribute to predictive modeling efforts, including early identification of at-risk learners and competency progression analytics. This is a high-ownership, foundational role. You'll shape AI strategy and implementation from the ground up, taking features from concept through production deployment. You'll work closely with educational leadership to identify opportunities where AI can meaningfully improve how we train future physicians. items.description: About Pivotal Health Pivotal Health is the leading technology platform that helps healthcare providers get paid fairly in an increasingly complex reimbursement landscape. Today, many providers face persistent underpayment from health insurance companies, despite delivering high-quality care. While processes like IDR (Independent Dispute Resolution) were designed to promote fairness, theyâre often administrative-heavy, time-consuming, and difficult to navigate without the right tools. Pivotal Health combines software, data, and service into a seamlessly integrated, AI-driven platform that simplifies these complex reimbursement workflows. We help providers efficiently dispute underpaid claims, reduce administrative burden, and recover the reimbursement theyâre entitled to; without adding more work to already stretched teams. Our full-service IDR solution is just the starting point. Weâre building solutions that enable providers to operate with clarity, control, and confidence across the reimbursement journey. About the Role We're hiring a Senior Software Engineer to join Pivotal's Case Execution team. This team owns critical parts of the case execution workflow, including eligibility, batching, submissions, ops workflows, and claim orchestration. These systems sit at the operational core of how Pivotal delivers outcomes for providers. This is a strong fit for an engineer who enjoys solving complex, workflow-driven backend problems and working through data-heavy decision logic. The most technically demanding areas for this team are eligibility and batching, and the right person is energized by that kind of work rather than looking to avoid it. What You'll Do Build and improve core case execution systems: Own backend development across eligibility, batching, submissions, ops workflows, and claim orchestration. These are the systems that determine how cases move through Pivotal's platform and reach resolution. Tackle complex, data-driven backend problems: Work through the decision logic and data-heavy workflows that make eligibility and batching hard, understanding not just how individual systems work, but how they interact across the broader platform. Contribute to workflow orchestration: Build and improve the systems that coordinate how cases are staged, routed, and executed end to end, with a clear eye toward correctness and reliability. You might be an: - AI Architect - AI Engineer - MLOps - Deep Learning Engineer - Data Scientist - Applied AI Engineer - ML Engineer - AI Researcher - Staff+ Engineer focused on AI - Technical founder with deep AI experience What matters is a track record of building and shipping.
